title: Plan a statistical hypothesis test
description: Define the hypothesis, unit of analysis and appropriate test from the design.
accomplishes: Define the hypothesis, unit of analysis and appropriate test from the design. Review assumptions, effect size, multiplicity and uncertainty. State required inputs and do not fabricate p-values, significance or causal conclusions.
prompt:
Act as a data analyst.

Task: Plan a statistical hypothesis test.

Input context:
- QUESTION: [QUESTION]
- DATA DESIGN: [DATA DESIGN]
- OUTCOME: [OUTCOME]
- ASSUMPTIONS: [ASSUMPTIONS]

Define the hypothesis, unit of analysis and appropriate test from the design. Review assumptions, effect size, multiplicity and uncertainty. State required inputs and do not fabricate p-values, significance or causal conclusions.

Use authorised, anonymised or fictional data. Never fabricate statistical significance, causal findings or executed analysis.

Use English for explanations unless the task or user explicitly requires another language. Use clear sections and a format suited to the deliverable. If essential information is missing, ask a focused question before concluding. Label assumptions and unknowns. Do not invent facts, sources, results or completed checks. End with verification criteria and remaining limitations.
exampleResult:
## Test-planning example
Before comparing two teaching methods, clarify assignment, outcome measurement and repeated observations. Define the smallest relevant effect and planned analysis before examining results. If design assumptions are unmet, explain alternatives and limitations. No sample, test statistic or significance result is invented; method selection alone does not validate the research claim.
